name: Tonbo Imaging India Ltd
title: Tonbo Imaging India Ltd - 544999 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Tonbo's H1 FY27 revenue of ₹219 cr is lumpy (Q1 ₹36 cr, Q2 ₹183 cr) with no formal guidance; management pushes annual framing while order book stands at ₹250 cr and ₹408 cr is under negotiation.

triggers.label: Order book ₹250 cr, ₹408 cr under negotiation
triggers.quote: Our current order book of about 250 crores together with contracts and the negotiation of about 408 crores

triggers.label: No revenue or margin guidance given
triggers.quote: I don't think there's going to be giving any guidance either on revenue or margins at this stage.

triggers.label: Export gross margin 60-65% vs domestic tactical 40-45%
triggers.quote: It will be anywhere in the 60 to 65 percent area on the export side.

guidance.quote: we believe that H2 revenues for this financial year are likely to be materially better than H1.

red_flags.label: Q2-heavy revenue; H1 EBITDA 14.2% with PAT ₹5.8 cr
red_flags.quote: Profit after tax was 5.8 crores for H2 with a Pact margin of 2.61 percent.

red_flags.label: Directed energy at TRL4; ₹160 cr first system funded by debt and grant
red_flags.quote: the rough cost of capital to build it is about 160 crores.

red_flags.label: Management asserts annual-only evaluation; avoids quarterly guidance
red_flags.quote: neither quarterly or sevy annual would do justice to evaluating the merits of the business.

evasions.quote: No, I can't comment on that.

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue of ₹219 crore, with Q2 at ₹183 crore driving the half; management guides H2 "materially better" than H1 but gives no formal guidance.
summary.overview: Tonbo Imaging's first analyst call after its recent IPO covered H1/Q2 FY27 results. Revenue from operations was ₹219 crore for H1 (vs ₹77 crore in H1 FY26), with Q1 at ₹36 crore and Q2 at ₹183 crore. Q2 EBITDA was ₹44 crore (24.11% margin) against H1 EBITDA of ₹31.15 crore (14.2%), and Q2 PAT was ₹23.5 crore. Management repeatedly asked investors to judge the business on an annual basis because quarterly revenue recognition is lumpy, and declined to give revenue or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: gross profit up ~87% vs ₹40 crore in H1 FY26; margin below 51% in FY26 due to product mix
management referred to this as H2; figure appears to be H1 given context

segments.name: Tactical systems
segments.commentary: Thermal weapon sites, binoculars and monoculars; about 70-80% of business per management. Domestic tactical gross margin ~40-45%; tactical orders convert in 3-6 months. About 250 crore of the 408 crore contracts under negotiation are tactical.

segments.name: Platform systems
segments.commentary: Gimbals, fire control systems, RCWS, seekers and EO for platforms; expected to grow in share over time. Domestic platform gross margin ~45-50%; delivery takes 6-18 months. About 150 crore of the 408 crore under negotiation is platform; most of the 250 crore order book is platform-related.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 35% of H1 revenue (65% domestic). Export gross margin ~60-65%. Management said about ₹61.5 crore of Q2 revenue came from the US, which it described as platform subsystems.

segments.name: Directed energy (HPM)
segments.commentary: Still development at TRL 4; ~₹160 crore first-system build cost funded by ₹120 crore loan (sanctioned), ₹25 crore IDEX-ADITI grant and ₹15 crore internal accruals. LOIs for 11 units (5 Indian Navy, 6 European). First deliveries expected FY29-30.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance; management cited the recent IPO as a restriction.
H2 FY27 revenue expected to be materially higher than H1, supported by the ₹250 crore order book, ₹408 crore under negotiation and a pipeline expected to convert within 2-3 months.
Management expects of the order book converting in FY27 about ₹100-200 crore, with the excess carried into FY28.
EBITDA margin expected to be above H1's 14.2% for the full year on higher revenue, better export mix and operating leverage.
R&D spend for FY27 about ₹30 crore (about ₹25 crore capitalised); HPM project cost ~₹150-160 crore over ~2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is outsourced to certified partners (asset-light model); capital is directed to R&D and IP rather than factories.
Tactical subsystems are kept pre-assembled in inventory, allowing tactical orders received by December to convert to revenue within 3-4 months.
Over 130 R&D engineers; 15+ years of R&D; 100% proprietary IP per management.
Bank cash credit limit raised from ₹30 crore to ₹50 crore post quarter-end with one bank; talks ongoing with the other two banks.
HPM first system capitalisation expected after customer intent is established; about ₹20 crore of employee cost capitalised for HPM over 2.5 years.
demand_pricing: India thermal weapon sites: ~80,000 thermal weapon sites and ~27,000 image intensifier sites in the tactical opportunity, largely via OCPP (procurement timeline under 12 months). Management said India's installed base is roughly 20,000-30,000 sites.
Tonbo claims ~65% market share in thermal weapon sites in India (20,000 of ~30,000 deployed); expects share to moderate to ~50% as the market grows.
International near-term tactical opportunity of about 10,000 thermal sites and monoculars.

European export order: first-order production units for a multi-sensor stabilised seeker for a state-owned company; option for up to €13 million on acceptance. Included in the ₹408 crore contracts under negotiation, not in the ₹250 crore order book.
HPM pricing: ~₹200 crore per system quoted to Indian Navy; ~$25 million per unit for international customers.
Competitors named: Bharat Electronics, Tata and Alpha Design in India; Epirus internationally in directed energy.

qa_highlights.question: How does the HPM market size differ between figures cited (~$290 million India by 2030 vs ~₹28,000 crore implied from 140 systems)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹28,000 crore figure is the total Indian addressable base at ~₹200 crore per system for ~140 systems, while the ~$290 million figure corresponds to FY30 expected procurement, which is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the competitors in directed energy and how does addressable scale compare with Epirus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Epirus is the only credible competitor with data; Tonbo aims for 3-5 km range, which Epirus does not offer to most export countries, and says it can compete in the same markets (Japan discussions noted).

qa_highlights.question: What are gross margins for tactical vs platform, domestic vs export?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic tactical ~40-45%; domestic platform ~45-50%; export ~60-65% without separating tactical and platform.

qa_highlights.question: Does the €13 million export option sit in the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is part of the ₹408 crore contracts under negotiation, not the ₹250 crore order book; management expects conversion if product meets specifications.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ₹250 crore order book convert and what is the FY27 revenue path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ~₹100-200 crore of the order book may execute this year, with the rest carried forward; ₹408 crore under negotiation assumed to convert by December.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 80,000 thermal site opportunity under serial production or capital procurement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly OCPP (fast, under 12 months), with some capital procurement in RFI/RFP stage taking 1.5 years for trials.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capitalisation policy for R&D?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 R&D of ~₹16 crore, of which ~₹3 crore expensed and rest capitalised; FY27 expected ~₹30 crore, ~₹25 crore capitalised. Blue-sky research is expensed; product development after customer intent is capitalised.

risks_watch: Quarterly revenue volatility: Q1 ₹36 crore vs Q2 ₹183 crore; FY26 H2 was 78% of revenue. Whether H2 is materially above H1 is the key near-term test.
Conversion of ₹408 crore under negotiation and pipeline by December; a slip pushes revenue into FY28.
HPM program: TRL 4, first deliveries FY29-30, ₹160 crore build cost; product engineering and testing risk.
Gross margin fell to 34.62% in H1 from 51% in FY26 due to mix; sustainability of margin recovery.
Working capital reliance: bank borrowings ₹169 crore; cash credit limits being expanded with other banks.
Export exposure, including US platform subsystem sales, and sensitivity to geopolitics and export controls.
Recent IPO limits guidance; investor reliance on annual rather than quarterly numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term opportunity and order pipeline but cautious and deliberately non-committal on near-term numbers, repeatedly declining revenue or margin guidance and steering investors to annual metrics. Management was more specific on product technology and programme structure than on timing.
key_quotes: Our promise is to democratize autonomy at the performance level military's need and at a cost that enables global scale.
While the market direction is clear that there will be increased acceptance and demand for products that enable battlefield autonomy, it is very difficult to predict timelines.
I don't think there's going to be giving any guidance either on revenue or margins at this stage.

growth.why: Management qualitatively guides H2 FY27 revenue materially above H1 (₹219 cr), backed by a ₹250 cr order book and ₹408 cr under negotiation, with ~₹100-200 cr of order book expected to convert in FY27; no formal numeric guidance and no company-owned capacity additions (manufacturing is outsourced).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects full-year EBITDA margin above H1's 14.2% on higher revenue, better export mix (export gross margin ~60-65% vs domestic ~40-50%) and operating leverage; Q2 EBITDA margin was already 24.11%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Manufacturing is outsourced to certified partners (asset-light), with capital directed to R&D and IP rather than factories; no company-owned capacity addition is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue materially above H1 (₹219 crore), backed by a ₹250 crore order book, ~₹100-200 crore expected to convert in FY27, and ₹408 crore under negotiation converting within 2-3 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with outsourced manufacturing; capital goes to R&D, and the HPM first-system build (~₹160 crore) is funded by a ₹120 crore sanctioned loan, ₹25 crore grant and ₹15 crore accruals rather than a new capex programme.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no formal numeric guidance (citing the recent IPO) but qualitatively expects H2 revenue materially above H1, so any upgrade would depend on order conversion by December.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Slippage in converting the ₹408 crore under negotiation by December would push revenue into FY28, and quarterly revenue is lumpy (Q1 ₹36 crore vs Q2 ₹183 crore).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Directed energy (HPM) is at TRL 4 with first deliveries expected FY29-30 and LOIs for 11 units; no near-term product launch date within the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: ₹408 crore contracts under negotiation converting
rows.why: Of the ₹408 crore under negotiation (₹250 crore tactical, ₹150 crore platform, with the €13 million European option included), management assumes conversion by December, but a slip pushes revenue into FY28.

rows.label: Cash credit limit expansion with banks
rows.why: One bank raised cash credit from ₹30 crore to ₹50 crore post quarter-end and talks continue with the other two banks, against bank borrowings of ₹169 crore that are mainly self-liquidating working capital.

rows.label: International tactical and directed-energy export demand
rows.why: Exports were about 35% of H1 revenue at ~60-65% gross margin, and about 10,000 international thermal sites are addressable, but US platform sales and export controls add geopolitical risk.

tone.note: Management was confident about the long-term opportunity, the ₹250 crore order book and H2 being materially above H1, but declined numeric guidance and steered investors to annual metrics; analysts pressed on the quarterly lumpiness and the HPM market sizing and competition.
